correctness.rationale: Unique smooth normal parameterization of the difference body has Jacobian m-s. A two-body C^3 tangency graph gives overlap (4/3)sqrt(2/q)s^(3/2)+O(s²) uniformly; inversion yields depth c q^(1/3) ε^(2/3)+O(ε). Integrating tube area proves the exact normal density and beta-angle independence. Sum-and-product algebra recovers unordered curvature radii. Finally, equality with affine arclength means mq constant, i.e., curvature-radius ratio r+1/r constant; continuity and support-function ODE imply reflected homothety. Numerical disk/ellipse computations corroborate coefficients but are not infinite proof.

value.rationale: The main question is physically and geometrically natural: what do exceptionally small intersection lenses reveal about both body boundaries? The joint law gives a universal conditional depth distribution and an orientation-resolved curvature statistic. Unlike a one-body scalar tail, its inverse distinguishes the unordered pair of local boundary curvature radii; equality of its conditional angle law with affine arclength rigidly characterizes homothetic reflected pairs. These are substantive structural and inverse properties, not arbitrary numerical invariants.
